A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same transformer counting study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: V1 reports original training experiments, accuracy measurements, model introspection and supplementary sensitivity studies, including five-run results in Figure 1 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains original training results, mechanistic probes, frozen-embedding comparisons and initialization-variability measurements in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The six architectures, attention mechanisms, residual connections, feed-forward network, training objective and two counting strategies remain unchanged. V2's uniform linear-mixing construction already appears in v1 Appendix A.3.1; the substantive mathematical revisions concern feasibility guarantees.

E1.justification: V2 removes the longer-sequence L = 15 evaluation from v1 Appendix D.5 and omits its briefly reported preliminary exploration of arbitrary objects with T = infinity. The finite-alphabet histogram task remains, and T = 64 is still represented in selected mechanistic examples.

E2.justification: Corresponding retained comparisons use the same six variants: lin, dot and bos, each with and without softmax. No comparison method is added, substituted or selectively removed from those comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 removes the systematic T = 64 evaluation over d and p in {2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128}, while retaining selected T = 64 diagnostic configurations. Retained experiments preserve the sampling procedure, Adam learning rate, 500-epoch budget, batch size and training/evaluation sample counts.

E4.justification: V1 Appendix D.4–D.5 tested sensitivity to alphabet size and sequence length, supporting the proposed dependence of transitions on T rather than L; these studies disappear. The frozen-embedding ablation, BOS mixing probes, confusion matrices, output-neuron analysis and singular-value analysis remain. The latter moves to v2 Appendix D.5.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over five runs, best-run results and standard deviations across five random initializations. The retained uncertainty reporting is unchanged; no additional runs, confidence intervals or significance procedures are documented.

E6.justification: Retained plotted results are unchanged, including the 99.9%, 99.47% and 99.97% accuracies in Figures 3–5. V2 removes the T = 64 and L = 15 sweep results and the preliminary arbitrary-object failure report. It newly reports a d = 12 dot construction with mutual coherence 0.299, and revises the description of the unchanged overlap/confusion plot to emphasize overcounting and narrower overlap distributions at smaller d.

T1.justification: Appendix B substantively revises the non-orthogonal feasibility analysis, adding residual-overlap and ReLU conditions and tightening the dot/bos p = T bound from a 2L−3 dependence to L−1. Proposition 4.4 states an L ≥ 5 restriction. The constant-dimension bos+sftm claim is corrected from d = 2 to d = 4. However, v2 reports a bound of 7 for T = 32, L = 10 although its revised formula evaluates to 8.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims about relation-based versus inventory-based counting, their efficiency difference, architectural interactions and empirical emergence. V2 foregrounds the theoretical-versus-learned gap for very small embeddings, but that distinction already appears in v1 Section 5.2 and Appendix B.3.1.

C2.justification: V2 more explicitly separates ideal Welch-bound predictions from constructions the authors could obtain, replacing v1's simpler emphasis on agreement with experiments. It expands the discussion of sequence-length-dependent margins and finite-precision failure, and removes the arbitrary-object generalization discussion. The principal limitations concerning single-layer, non-autoregressive models remain.

D1.justification: V2 gives more specific descriptions of executable PyTorch constructions for named propositions, the d = 4 case and the d = 12 example. The repository address, empirical hyperparameters and Appendix C data-generation instructions remain unchanged. This establishes expanded reproducibility documentation, without establishing an external repository update.

R1.justification: Gurnee et al. (2023), Finding Neurons in a Haystack, and Reddy (2024), on in-context classification, disappear with the shortened future-work discussion. The main related-work coverage and positioning relative to RASP, memorization and algorithmic alignment remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract and contribution list, substantially restructures the results exposition around numbered propositions and counting-strategy subsections, moves Related Work after the results, and merges limitations and conclusions. Appendix constructions are reorganized into explicitly identified proofs, with extensive accompanying prose revisions.

P2.justification: V1 Figures 13–14 are removed, and its singular-value Figure 6 moves to v2 Appendix D as Figure 13. The scalar-to-category illustration changes from a wrapped placement to a standalone display, with additional caption and spacing adjustments. Every retained figure preserves its underlying graphic.

improvement.justification: Corrections to residual-overlap/ReLU reasoning and the d = 4 dimension accounting, together with clearer propositions and organization, provide a limited improvement in rigor and readability. Removing the alphabet-size and sequence-length sensitivity studies reduces empirical support for scaling, and the revised bound introduces a numerical inconsistency: the example reports 7 while the formula gives 8. These drawbacks temper the gains.
